Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11

Class X11CompositorSession

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.displayserver.nativewindow.x11.X11CompositorSession
public final class X11CompositorSession extends Object
The discovery seam that lets the conventional 2D desktop find a live X11 compositor session running in the same JVM, so it can host native X11 clients as ordinary MDI windows (Phase G of the compositor roadmap).

When lg3d runs as the X session — the window manager plus the Composite/Damage compositor on a bare Xorg — X11IntegrationModule publishes the session here once redirection succeeds. The 2D shell then reads current() and, if a session is live, wires a CompositedWindowBridge to it. In every other topology (dev mode, the *_nox configs, or compositing disabled) nothing is published and current() returns null, so the desktop is unchanged.

The published X11CompositorSession.Session deliberately exposes only the Java-3D-free interface types — a CompositedWindowHost and a WindowLifecycleRegistrar — never the concrete X11Compositor or the package-private X11WindowManager. So referencing this class from the desktop2d package drags in neither the scene graph nor gnu.x11; the concrete host is built here, on the X11 side, at publish time.

  • Method Details

    • publish

      public static void publish(X11Compositor compositor, WindowLifecycleRegistrar registrar)
      Publishes the live session, building the production X11CompositedWindowHost over the active compositor. A null argument is treated as "no session" and clears it, so a failed bring-up cannot leave a half-published session behind.
      Parameters:
      compositor - the active compositor (its display is already claimed)
      registrar - the window manager that fires lifecycle notifications
